newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH T-BILL YIELDS TO RISE AT MONDAY TENDER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH T-BILL YIELDS TO RISE AT MONDAY TENDER.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to rise at Monday's tender after the Treasury let T-bond yields rise this week, but even this may not lure larger foreign capital back into Polish paper ahead of next month's elections.

Dealers said that T-bill yields should rise between 10 and 35 basis points at Monday's 1.1 billion zloty primary tender, with demand focused on shorter eight and 13-week bills after the central bank raised official interest rates this week.
The National Bank of Poland raised its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and its discount by 2.5 to 24.5 percent.

"T-bill yields should rise after (fixed 15-percent) two-year bonds rose to around 23.7 percent at Wednesday's tender...but foreigners are not likely to be very active ahead of parliamentary polls, unless the zloty swings," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers expect T-bill yields to continue to gradually rise until foreign investors, wary of political uncertainty and a weak zloty, return to Poland and knock them down.

"If foreigners return in large numbers yields could drop by as much as 30 to 40 bp per week, but such inflows are not expected for roughly about two months," said Marcin Dec, dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
Dealers said however that Polish yields were so attractive that some shorter-term foreign investors could buy T-bills.
"Foreigners may place some bids (on Monday) especially for short-term paper...but its likely to be linked to zloty speculation," said Artur Wrobel, dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Dealers said that after weeks of withdrawal, foreign investors had depleted Polish T-bill portfolios, signalling that the zloty would probably stay around present levels until the next larger capital flow occured.
They said the zloty would remain range-bound between minus 0.5 and 1.3 percent from the parity rate next week.

"The perception of the market is that the central bank is guarding support at minus 1.5 percent and the zloty bounced up on Friday and may rise to minus 0.5 before easing again," said Witold Wozniak, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
The zloty closed the week at -0.74 percent, up from Thursday's low at -1.16 percent and slightly higher than last week's close at -0.87 percent.
It was at 3.4880 to the dollar and 1.8735 to the mark.
One-day rates on the money market were expected to remain locked next week around 23 percent, the level of the central bank's benchmark 14-day reverse repo operation.
